questions.question: Given that [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix} -5 & -3\\ 2&0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex] and [latex]I=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0\\ 0&1 \end{bmatrix}[/latex], the value of [latex]A^{3}[/latex] is
questions.explanation: [latex]A=\left[\begin{array}{rr}-5 & -3 \\ 2 & 0\end{array}\right] \text{ and } I=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right] [/latex] Characteristic equation of A is [latex] \begin{aligned} \left|\begin{array}{rr}-5-\lambda & -3 \\ 2 & 0-\lambda\end{array}\right|&=0\\ (-5-\lambda)(-\lambda)+6&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \lambda^{2}+5 \lambda+6&=0 \\ \text{ So,}\quad A^{2}+5 A+6 I&=0 \\ &\text{(by Cayley Hamilton theorem) }\\ \Rightarrow \quad A^{2}=-5 A-6 I& \end{aligned}[/latex] Multiplying by A on both sides, we have, [latex] \begin{aligned} A^{3} &=-5 A^{2}-6 A \\ \Rightarrow \quad A^{3} &=-5(-5 A-6 I)-6 A \\ &=19 A+30I \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]A=\left[\begin{array}{rr}-5 & -3 \\ 2 & 0\end{array}\right] \text{ and } I=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right] [/latex]
Characteristic equation of A is
[latex] \begin{aligned} \left|\begin{array}{rr}-5-\lambda & -3 \\ 2 & 0-\lambda\end{array}\right|&=0\\ (-5-\lambda)(-\lambda)+6&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \lambda^{2}+5 \lambda+6&=0 \\ \text{ So,}\quad A^{2}+5 A+6 I&=0 \\ &\text{(by Cayley Hamilton theorem) }\\ \Rightarrow \quad A^{2}=-5 A-6 I& \end{aligned}[/latex]
Multiplying by A on both sides, we have,
[latex] \begin{aligned} A^{3} &=-5 A^{2}-6 A \\ \Rightarrow \quad A^{3} &=-5(-5 A-6 I)-6 A \\ &=19 A+30I \end{aligned}[/latex]
